identified_issues: Improper authorization and privilege escalation resulting from coarse permission aggregation
Erasure of distinct security boundaries between interactive sessions and batch execution workflows
Violation of the principle of least privilege by granting the union of permissions to all session contexts
evidence: Workflow A definition restricts permitted actions to { READ, EXPORT_DRAFT, REQUEST_APPROVAL }
Compression middleware maps distinct workflows into a single session_type 'AUTHORIZED_USER_SESSION' with combined_permissions containing the union of all actions
The middleware approved an EXECUTE_MUTATION action submitted by an interactive operator in Workflow A because EXECUTE_MUTATION was included in the flattened combined_permissions array
recommended_action: Refactor the caching middleware to eliminate permission aggregation. Maintain distinct context models that preserve granular session types and enforce workflow-specific permission sets independently, ensuring that interactive sessions cannot access mutation execution capabilities.
